Attached: Cardia_Eval_Scope.pdf (3 pages)

Key asks from CardiaLabs:

Marissa — looping in capacity notes and tradeoffs (attached). I'm flagging two things that will push their decision one way or the other:

1) Cost & utilization profile
- Hosted (start): lowest lead time, unit cost moderate. For 100k qpm P95 pattern with bursty peak, hosted is simplest to spin up and measure (we can throttle).
- Dedicated: better predictable unit cost if they commit to a monthly baseline; lead time 3–5 weeks to reserve a pool (depends on GPU type and region).
- Private: highest engineering lead time and procurement friction (VPNs/KMS/HSM setup) but best for absolute data control.

2) Regional compliance vs latency
- For EU PHI concerns, recommending eu-west (Ireland) for primary inference and us-east as DR. We can limit KV persistence to eu-west. If they need on-prem PHI controls, Private is required.

3) Fallback strategy
- Propose a MAP clause: start hosted in eu-west with a Dedicated reservation warm standby (kept in the plan, provisioned post-PO). If Dedicated lead time hits procurement, we can keep hosted but configure KV restrictions and a telemetry-only export for audit.

Attached: capacity_estimates.csv (csv)

I recommend we include a single-line procurement-friendly commitment: a 30-day SLA for capacity provisioning after PO for Dedicated, with a clearly defined migration window to Private (30–90 days depending on KMS work). Ben — can you draft the SOW language around that?

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
